source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) Are Diagnostic Concepts Within the Reach of LLMs? (DX 2025)
finding: Tests whether LLMs can do the structural-analysis core of model-based diagnosis: build incidence matrices, find Minimal Structurally Overdetermined (MSO) sets, conflicts, and minimal diagnoses for logic and arithmetic circuits. MSO sets are the structural basis of detectability and isolability.
numbers: 23 circuits (adders, multipliers, AND/OR/NOR/NAND/XOR). Models gpt-4o-mini (with code interpreter), o1, o3-mini. 10 repeats per case for 4o-mini and o3-mini; o1 once (about 30 USD per iteration). Each step scored with correct inputs given.
limits: Small circuits (up to 29 unknowns, 15 relations). Ground truth from Fault Diagnosis Toolbox. Models were not tested on the diagnosability verdict itself.
agent_relevance: LLMs can approximate the formal steps behind diagnosability, but need a symbolic checker for anything beyond small cases.

source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) Are Diagnostic Concepts Within the Reach of LLMs? (DX 2025) - incidence matrix step
finding: Incidence matrix generation (which unknowns appear in which equation) is the easy step: o1 and o3-mini got it perfect, 4o-mini added known variables and faults.
numbers: o1 and o3-mini: F1 1.00, strict accuracy 1.00. 4o-mini: F1 0.47, precision 0.33, strict accuracy 0.00 (read from figure labels).
limits: Strict accuracy needs exact variable sets per equation. Figure values read from extracted text.
agent_relevance: Structure extraction from a given model is reliable for reasoning models; weaker non-reasoning models over-include variables.

source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) Are Diagnostic Concepts Within the Reach of LLMs? (DX 2025) - MSO, conflicts, diagnoses
finding: Performance falls as the task gets more combinatorial. MSO generation drops with more relations and more MSOs for o1 and o3-mini; diagnosis generation (minimal hitting sets) shows the clearest decline with complexity. A dedicated prompt with domain knowledge was no better than a broad prompt.
numbers: o3-mini conflicts F1 = 0.917 +/- 0.249; o3-mini diagnoses F1 = 0.784 +/- 0.322. o1 best on conflicts; o3-mini best on diagnoses. Dedicated vs broad prompts: similar scores. Supplying the correct incidence matrix did not help MSO generation significantly.
quote: As LLMs were not primarily designed to handle algorithmic and computational tasks, the performance of reasoning models is surprisingly good.
limits: Examples were written by hand and solutions released after the models, so contamination is unlikely. Conflict trend with complexity is inflated by zero-conflict cases where models fail.
agent_relevance: Hitting-set step is where LLMs break. Put the hitting set and the isolability check in code (S5/S7), not in the chain of thought. Extra domain knowledge in the prompt did not buy accuracy.

source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) Are Diagnostic Concepts Within the Reach of LLMs? (DX 2025) - definitions and model comparison
finding: Gives the structural definitions: a fault is detectable if some fault-MSO set contains it; fault f is isolable from f' if some FMSO contains f but not f'. Without a code interpreter, gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini scored close to zero on unseen examples; only 4o-mini with code interpreter was run in full.
numbers: gpt-4o / 4o-mini without interpreter: accuracy near zero on unseen circuits. Reasoning models o1 and o3-mini: high effort for the Dedicated approach, medium for the Broad one.
limits: The authors cannot rule out that o1 and o3-mini used a hidden interpreter.
agent_relevance: Tool use (code execution) matters more than model size for combinatorial diagnosis steps.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Uncertainty of Thoughts: Uncertainty-Aware Planning Enhances Information Seeking in LLMs
finding: UoT simulates future question/answer trees and scores each question by expected uncertainty reduction (entropy of the yes/no split of the remaining candidate set). It is test selection by information gain in an LLM loop, on 20 Questions, medical diagnosis and troubleshooting.
numbers: 5 datasets: Common (111 items), Things (1854), DX (104 dialogues), MedDG (500), FloDial (894 dialogues, 153 faults). GPT-4, closed set success: UoT 71.2 / 37.5 / 97.0 / 88.0 / 67.3 vs direct prompting 50.5 / 30.5 / 91.3 / 72.3 / 43.7. Average gain 38.1% in success rate over direct prompting; Llama3-70B largest at 46.6%.
limits: Assumes answer sets are disjoint and the candidate set is given (closed set). Simulated answerer is an LLM; humans checked 10% (final judgments 100%, intermediate 92.9-94.4%). Page read to 100k of 115k characters.
agent_relevance: Direct analogue of S7: choose the test that best splits the live hypotheses. Works best when the hypothesis set is explicit.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Uncertainty of Thoughts: Uncertainty-Aware Planning Enhances Information Seeking in LLMs - open set
finding: When the candidate list is not given (open set), gains are smaller and absolute scores are low.
numbers: GPT-4 open set: direct prompting 48.6 / 16.5 / 44.2 / 45.7 / 38.4 vs UoT 55.3 / 28.0 / 49.1 / 67.4 / 43.5 (Common / Things / DX / MedDG / FloDial).
limits: Same caveats as above.
agent_relevance: Where the suspect set is not enumerated, test selection is weak. Generating the suspect list is the bottleneck.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Uncertainty of Thoughts: Uncertainty-Aware Planning Enhances Information Seeking in LLMs - ablations and cost
finding: The uncertainty reward is what helps: adding it to Tree-of-Thoughts improves planning by about 5.9% on average, and removing it from UoT lowers results. Gains persist at matched token cost. Reflection without a test-value score can hurt.
numbers: Matched cost (GPT-4, ~9.2k tokens): UoT 54.4 / 92.5 / 66.0 (20Q / medical / troubleshooting) vs Adapted-ToT D=3 (4.5k tokens) 33.8 / 85.1 / 60.3. UoT beats CoT-SC by 33.8%, Reflexion by 29.9%, Original-ToT by 28.3%, Adapted-ToT by 12.4% on average. All-path propagation 71.2 vs CRPS 68.5 vs UoT-Max 63.7 (Common, GPT-4). Reflexion scored 52.5 on DX and 30.3 on MedDG vs direct prompting 91.3 and 72.3.
limits: Depth fixed at 3 for budget. Authors suggest Bayesian updating as future work.
agent_relevance: A numeric split score is a cheap guardrail for test choice; free-form reflection is not.

source: Choudhury and Williamson (2025) BED-LLM: Intelligent Information Gathering with LLMs and Bayesian Experimental Design
finding: Treats each question as an experiment: sample hypotheses from the LLM, filter those inconsistent with answers so far, estimate expected information gain (EIG) with the LLM's probabilities, ask the best question. Large gains on 20 Questions over letting the LLM ask freely.
numbers: 20 Questions success at final turn (Prompt-only / Split / BED-LLM): Animals GPT-4o 45/83/93; Animals Mistral-Large 33/85/95; Animals Llama-3.1-8B 8/49/63; Celebrities GPT-4o 45/63/86; Things GPT-4o 34/40/64. Average gain 37.4 points over prompt-only. 100 targets per dataset, 20 questions.
limits: Two task families only. Conditional question generation can overfit to the sampled hypothesis set. Predictive entropy alone is a poor stand-in for EIG. Preference task scored by an LLM judge. Page read to 100k of 160k characters.
agent_relevance: Even a plain split-the-hypotheses heuristic gives most of the gain (Split 83 vs Prompt-only 45 on Animals GPT-4o). Keep an explicit, filtered hypothesis list and rank tests by how they split it.

source: Choudhury and Williamson (2025) BED-LLM: Intelligent Information Gathering with LLMs and Bayesian Experimental Design - ablations
finding: Ablations show which parts matter. Keeping beliefs only in the prompt context fails badly; explicit hypothesis sets with filtering work.
numbers: GPT-4o Animals: BED-LLM 93; Entropy 88; Data-Est. 70; ICL Beliefs 25; Implicit Max. 70; CoT 62; Prompt-only 45.
limits: Appendix not read.
agent_relevance: Beliefs held only in the prompt (ICL Beliefs 25) were worse than no scaffold. Hypotheses must be an explicit data structure.

source: Shoot First, Ask Questions Later? Building Rational Agents that Explore and Act Like People (2025), Battleship
finding: Collaborative Battleship: a Captain asks yes/no questions to a Spotter. Computing expected information gain over sampled boards, with question answering by generated code, lifts weak models above humans and a stronger model.
numbers: Human study 42 people, 126 games. Spotter accuracy: humans 92.5%; Llama-4-Scout 62.2%; range across 15 LMs 52.5% to 92.8%; code answering +13.2 points. Targeting F1 LM-only to full Bayesian: Llama-4-Scout 0.367 to 0.764, GPT-4o 0.450 to 0.782 (GPT-5 LM-only 0.716). Redundant (EIG=0) questions: Llama-4-Scout 18.5% to 0.2%, GPT-4o 14.6% to 1.2%. Win rate vs humans about 0.82-0.83; vs GPT-5 0.67; cost about 1% of GPT-5 for Llama-4-Scout.
limits: World model is hand-built for Battleship. Fixed noise epsilon 0.1. Captain evaluation uses a fixed GPT-5 Spotter. Page read to 100k of 181k characters; authors not read.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that models waste questions (14-18% had zero information gain) and that a code-side EIG filter removes the waste.

source: Cloud-OpsBench (2026) Kubernetes RCA benchmark, arXiv 2603.00468
finding: Scores agents on outcome AND investigation process. Many correct diagnoses come from incomplete evidence: the agent names the right component without tracing the cause.
numbers: 11 LLMs (GPT-5, Claude-Sonnet-4, Gemini-2.5-Pro, others). 452 fault cases, 40 root-cause types. Mean JRA 0.59 (OnlineBoutique), 0.49 (TrainTicket). GPT-5: correct but evidence-incomplete in 33.1% (OnlineBoutique) and 29.4% (TrainTicket) of cases. Audit of 100 outcome-correct unclosed runs: 73% stopped at a symptom log.
quote: strong outcome accuracy often masks incomplete investigations.
limits: Replay of captured snapshots only; other queries return empty, which bounds observability. Page read to 100k of 156k characters.
agent_relevance: Matches the diagnosability question: a verdict reached without a discriminating observation is a guess. Add a gate that requires a causal chain before accepting.

source: Cloud-OpsBench (2026) Kubernetes RCA benchmark, arXiv 2603.00468 - failure modes and observability
finding: Four failure families: evidence grounding (anchoring on noisy downstream symptoms), search control (stopping early, repeating queries), target resolution (blaming the caller instead of the shared database), tool grounding. Some faults are not distinguishable from the available telemetry.
numbers: GPT-5 JRA 0.00 on Hard TrainTicket performance faults (pods look healthy). On OnlineBoutique, resource saturation from a ChaosBlade injection vs a code defect cannot be told apart without reading source. Qwen3-8B repeated earlier queries (RAR 0.45).
limits: Observed on two systems only.
agent_relevance: This is non-diagnosability in practice: two causes with the same observable signature. The agent should say it cannot separate X from Y with these observations and name the extra test needed.

source: Cloud-OpsBench (2026) Kubernetes RCA benchmark, arXiv 2603.00468 - scaffolds
finding: Scaffold comparison with GLM-5.1 at a 50-call budget: coding-agent harnesses beat plain ReAct on process quality, at higher token cost. In-context examples helped on one system, mixed on the other.
numbers: OnlineBoutique: Codex JRA 0.86 / ECR 0.83 / 126.29K tokens vs ReAct 0.81 / 0.68 / 55.13K. TrainTicket: Codex 0.67 / 0.81 / 205.17K; OpenCode 0.63 / 0.71 / 361.27K. ICL on OnlineBoutique: JRA 0.70 to 0.79, ECR 0.62 to 0.75.
limits: Single base model for the scaffold test. No ablation section.
agent_relevance: More structure raises evidence completeness (ECR) more than final-answer accuracy (JRA).

source: OpenRCA 2.0 (2026) PAVE step-wise causal annotation, arXiv 2606.27154
finding: Relabels RCA instances with the full cause-to-symptom path. Models often name a correct service but cannot show the path ('ungrounded diagnosis'). Strict exact-set scoring is low.
numbers: 500 instances, 11 frontier LLMs. Exact root-cause set recovered: 20.7% on average. At least one correct root-cause service: 76.0%. That service grounded in a verified causal path: 61.5%.
limits: Abstract-level page only; model names and failure taxonomy not read. Work in progress (v2, 30 Jun 2026).
agent_relevance: Multiple root causes and path grounding are the hard part. Score our agent on the full set of candidates consistent with the evidence, not one plausible guess.

source: ORCA-bench (2026) coding agents on oncall RCA, arXiv 2607.28545
finding: Production-like incident benchmark with hallucination tracked separately. Best accuracy is low, and removing source code access hurts all models and increases implausible causes.
numbers: 1,079 tasks (a secondary summary said 884; the abstract says 1,079). Five frontier agents. Best RCA accuracy 25.3% on Medium and 10.0% on Hard. Weakest model proposes an implausible root cause in 40% of reports. LLM judge vs humans weighted kappa 0.91.
limits: Abstract-level page. Unclear how multiple valid causes are credited.
agent_relevance: When observability is thin, models still commit to an answer (40% implausible). The agent needs an explicit insufficient-to-discriminate output.

source: How Far Can Root Cause Analysis Go on Real-World Telemetry Data? (2026) arXiv 2607.13548
finding: Rules mined from past audit reports and given to an RCA agent raise full score on a held-out cloud testbed. Deleting the earliest-onset criterion from a five-step procedure removes part of the gain. An audit found failures where a grounded evidence chain existed but the agent did not follow it.
numbers: OpenRCA held-out cloudbed full score: mined rules 14.10 to 35.90; manual rules 24.36; label-and-schema control 19.23. Rules add 17 solved cases with the procedure, 11 without. Deleting only earliest-onset: net gain 8 vs 11 for the full procedure. Removing the procedure raised full score in all three conditions but no contrast survived multiple-testing correction.
limits: Abstract-level page. The claim that accuracy is bounded, seen in a search summary, was NOT found on the page.
agent_relevance: Domain rules fed as precomputed evidence can more than double accuracy, but a fixed procedure did not reliably help once corrected for multiple tests.

source: Microsoft AI (2025) Sequential Diagnosis with Language Models (MAI-DxO), arXiv 2506.22405
finding: Sequential diagnosis benchmark: findings are revealed only when the agent asks for them. An orchestrator that simulates a panel of physicians, keeps a differential, and picks high-value cheap tests beats physicians and plain o3.
numbers: SDBench: 304 NEJM case records. MAI-DxO with o3: 80% accuracy vs 20% for generalist physicians; 85.5% in max-accuracy configuration. Cost 20% below physicians and 70% below off-the-shelf o3. Gains hold across OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, Grok, DeepSeek, Llama families.
limits: Abstract-level page. Not peer reviewed. Physician comparison conditions not read.
agent_relevance: Scaffold effect on test selection is large: same base model, 4x gap to physicians, cost cut 70%. A differential plus cost-aware test choice is the working pattern.

source: Estevez, Astorga, van der Schaar (2025) ACTMED: Timely Clinical Diagnosis through Active Test Selection (NeurIPS 2025)
finding: LLM acts as a patient-state simulator; Bayesian experimental design picks the next test by expected reduction in diagnostic uncertainty; a KL-shift rule stops testing. Beats letting the LLM pick tests itself, and even a full-information baseline on hepatitis and diabetes.
numbers: Budget 3 tests per patient; datasets hepatitis C, diabetes, kidney disease, OSCE; about 1,000 patients total; GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o; mean over 5 seeds. KL-based stopping cut average tests to under two (nearly 50% fewer) with equal or better accuracy.
limits: Binary classification only; about 1,000 patients; structured data only. More LLM queries than simple heuristics. Exact accuracy table values not extracted.
agent_relevance: A stop rule based on the expected shift in beliefs is a concrete way to decide that more tests will not separate the remaining suspects.

source: Estevez, Astorga, van der Schaar (2025) ACTMED: Timely Clinical Diagnosis through Active Test Selection (NeurIPS 2025) - implicit selection
finding: When the LLM picks tests itself, it keeps choosing the same globally useful tests for every patient; it does not adapt to the patient's current uncertainty.
numbers: In diabetes both models almost exclusively picked the globally optimal features, though ACTMED was more accurate. LLM-selected feature match rate to global optima is high with low variance.
limits: Shown in a figure; no single summary number extracted.
agent_relevance: Without a belief state, LLM test choice is a fixed habit, not a discrimination step.

source: Google DeepMind (2025) QuestBench: Can LLMs ask the right question to acquire information in reasoning tasks? arXiv 2503.22674
finding: Underspecified problems with exactly one missing variable; the model must pick the single question that makes the problem solvable. This tests whether the model can tell what is identifiable.
numbers: Logic-Q and Planning-Q: all models under 50%; GSM-Q and GSME-Q: over 80% for strong models, up to 99.39% (GSME-Q) and 84.05% (GSM-Q) on the full set. Models: GPT-4o, o1 Preview, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking. Accuracy correlates negatively with search-tree complexity (Spearman, Table 3).
limits: One missing variable only. Per-model table too garbled to quote cell by cell.
agent_relevance: Models solve a problem when fully specified but cannot tell which unknown blocks it. Need a code-side check of whether the answer is determined before answering.

source: Google DeepMind (2025) QuestBench: Can LLMs ask the right question to acquire information in reasoning tasks? arXiv 2503.22674 - filtering test
finding: Being good at solving the well-specified version does not predict being good at asking. After filtering to problems the model solves when fully specified, question-asking accuracy rose only slightly on Planning-Q and not at all on Logic-Q.
numbers: Question-asking accuracy changed by up to +39% for some models and about -10% for others on GSM variants after filtering; neither Logic-Q nor Planning-Q reached 100%.
limits: Described in the paper text; exact table not extracted.
agent_relevance: Solving and diagnosing what is missing are separate skills; do not assume one gives the other.

source: Shchekotykhin, Friedrich, Fleiss, Rodler (2012/2014) Interactive ontology debugging: two query strategies for efficient fault localization
finding: Older AI system: when many diagnoses explain the fault, ask an oracle yes/no questions about entailments that split the diagnoses. Entropy-based selection needs far fewer queries than split-in-half or random, even when all fault priors are equal.
numbers: Entropy-based beats split-in-half and random by more than 50% in queries (|Dt|=2 case); introduction says almost 60% better than random. A 33,000-axiom ontology resolved in 190 seconds with an average of 5 queries. Minimum possible is log2(n) queries with a perfect even split.
limits: Needs an oracle that answers truthfully; real users err. Test ontologies are generated examples plus real ones.
agent_relevance: Gold-standard test selection under non-diagnosability: ask the question whose answers partition the remaining diagnoses most evenly (log2 n bound).

source: Rodler (2020) DynamicHS: Streamlining Reiter's Hitting-Set Tree for Sequential Diagnosis, arXiv 2012.11078
finding: Sequential diagnosis loop: compute leading minimal diagnoses, pick a discriminating measurement, measure, repeat. DynamicHS keeps the search tree between iterations. A discriminating measurement point is one where every outcome rules out at least one leading diagnosis.
numbers: DynamicHS needed less time than HS-Tree in 96% of sessions; median and maximal savings 52% and 75%; in hardest cases it avoided median and maximal overheads of over 175% and 800%. Savings similar for entropy, split and MPS heuristics (median about 50%).
quote: proposing a discriminating measurement point... for each measurement outcome there must be at least one leading diagnosis that is inconsistent
limits: Evaluated on knowledge-based-system diagnosis problems only; HS-Tree was occasionally faster (86% less time in one scenario).
agent_relevance: Defines the operational test in a loop: if no discriminating measurement exists among leading diagnoses, the faults are not separable by that sensor set.

source: Failing to Falsify: Evaluating and Mitigating Confirmation Bias in Language Models (2026) arXiv 2604.02485
finding: Eleven LLMs on an interactive rule-discovery task (propose triples, get yes/no, guess the rule) often propose confirming rather than falsifying tests. Prompting to consider counterexamples helps; distilling that behaviour partly transfers to the Blicket test.
numbers: Average rule-discovery rate 42% to 56% with counterexample prompting (eleven LLMs). Blicket transfer called promising, no figure on page.
limits: Abstract-level page; model names and per-model rates not read.
agent_relevance: Tests that only confirm do not discriminate. Add a rule: each test must be able to rule out a live suspect.

source: Separable Pathways for Causal Reasoning: Architectural Scaffolding Enables Hypothesis-Space Restructuring in LLM Agents (2026) arXiv 2604.20039
finding: Blicket-style causal discovery where the hypothesis space must change mid-task. Typed state-machine exploration (context graphs) drives reasoning quality within the new space; dynamic behaviours that detect regime change prevent sticking with old hypotheses.
numbers: 1,085 trials; context graphs account for 94% of the accuracy gain after the switch. No absolute accuracies on page.
limits: Abstract-level page; models and baselines not named.
agent_relevance: If observations contradict all current suspects, the agent must widen the suspect set, not only re-weight it (the unknown-fault catch-all in diagnosis).

source: Towards LLM-based Root Cause Analysis of Hardware Design Failures (2025) arXiv 2507.06512
finding: LLMs explain buggy hardware design scenarios well when the full design and failure are given.
numbers: 34 buggy scenarios; o3-mini correct 100% of the time under pass@5; other models usually above 80%; with retrieval-augmented generation usually above 90%.
limits: pass@5 is lenient (a guess among five counts). Abstract-level page. Fully visible design, not partial observation.
agent_relevance: Shows the easy end: with full observability LLMs diagnose well. The failures above appear when observability drops.

source: Search summary: blicket-task biases and sequential BED (2025-2026)
finding: A search summary reports a disjunctive bias in LM agents on blicket tasks (infer disjunctive rules, fail on conjunctive ones) and that in a sequential-BED paper LLMs do not consistently beat random guessing when proposing experiments.
numbers: No figures seen.
limits: Seen only in a search result snippet, not opened. Treat as a lead.
agent_relevance: Check before relying on it.

source: Search summary: GALA graph-augmented multi-agent RCA (2025)
finding: GALA workflow was reported by search results at up to 42.22% Top-1 accuracy.
numbers: 42.22% Top-1 (secondary).
limits: Seen only in a search snippet; dataset differs from OpenRCA so numbers are not comparable.
agent_relevance: Lead only.
